key_insight: Machine learning interatomic potentials capture the rotational energy landscape of AESO fragments, helping connect localized orientational defects to dielectric relaxation during polymer curing.
engineering_relevance: Predicting which molecular rotations remain active as a bio-based polymer network forms could support interpretation of dielectric cure monitoring.
method: Measure dielectric permittivity at 500–5000 Hz during intermittent UV curing of AESO:VDM with DMPA photoinitiator.
Analyze relaxation dynamics using sliding-window Shannon entropy and Grassberger–Procaccia correlation integrals.
Compare MACE-OFF23 relaxed scans of five rotational modes against DFT profiles and estimate timescales with an Arrhenius model.
evidence_signal: MACE reproduces all five DFT profile shapes with Pearson r = 0.95–0.98 and preserves the barrier hierarchy; Arrhenius estimates place acrylate rotations closest to the dielectric measurement window.
watch_item: MACE underestimates barriers by 3–20%, and fragment-based scans with simple Arrhenius estimates do not establish rotational rates in the full curing network.
paper_title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
